statements.justification: All quoted values match and the contrasts are read correctly. Weak points: CAD9's 'amplified' induction is 0.21 log2; CCR2 stays below WT under drought (-0.47), so 'reinforced lignification' is thin; FAH1 is CYP84A1, not CYP84A4. Reading the F5H repression (-1.64) as a shift in monolignol composition is a fair, hedged hypothesis.

Values match: trehalose is high in BRL3ox at day 0 (+1.60) and rises less by day 5 (+0.60 vs +1.85), invertases are lower, SUS3 higher. Flaws: BFRUCT4 is the vacuolar, not cell-wall, invertase; 'TRE1 hub' is a network artifact (TRE1 unchanged); the paper reads the time course as steeper accumulation in BRL3ox.
statements.in_paper_where: Results 'BRL3ox plants accumulate osmoprotectant metabolites' (Fig. 4b, 4d) and the PaintOmics paragraph (Suppl. Fig. 11): trehalose and sucrose accumulation, deregulated sucrose metabolism. The invertase and TPS7 readings are not in the paper.

statements.justification: Values match, but glucose is one of the flagged metabolites: significantly lower in BRL3ox roots at day 0 (paper, Fig. 4b) with a different drought profile (Fig. 4j), so 'BRL3ox-independent' is wrong. The stomatal idea rests on HXK1 in tobacco guard cells; this is HKL1, a different non-catalytic protein, in roots.
statements.in_paper_where: Discussion names HKL1 among enzymes regulated by BRL3 overexpression; Results (Fig. 4b, 4j) say the opposite of the statement for glucose.

statements.justification: Values match and both sign flips are real: BGLU24 goes from -1.71 to +0.70 and has the largest drought-by-genotype difference of the pathway's relevant genes (also in the authors' interaction list). Linking BGLU24 to ABA-glucose-ester hydrolysis is by homology to BGLU18 only (leaf study), but it is offered as a possibility.

Values match (PYL4 -0.68, PYL5 -1.33, HAI3 +1.75 watered; same under drought) and it is correctly called a baseline difference, not a drought response. PYL6 and HAI1/HAI2 behave alike. This receptor-down, PP2C-up pattern gives the paper's 'constitutively activated ABA/stress genes' a concrete core-signalling basis the authors did not describe.
statements.in_paper_where: Results 'Transcriptional control of metabolite production in BRL3ox' (Fig. 5a-c, Suppl. Fig. 8): response-to-ABA genes deregulated at basal conditions. PYL and PP2C genes are not discussed.

statements.justification: Values match. SnRK2.7 and SnRK2.9 are higher in BRL3ox (clearly so under drought, +0.77 and +0.75) although drought lowers both; ABF2 is higher at baseline (+0.71). Descriptive, with textbook background; the cited ABF paper concerns SnRK2.2/2.3/2.6, not these two kinases. No interpretation is offered beyond the pattern.
statements.in_paper_where: Results (Fig. 5a-c, Suppl. Fig. 8): ABA response among the most altered in BRL3ox roots. These genes are not named.

statements.justification: Values match: MAPKKK18 is lower in watered BRL3ox (-1.39), the gap closes under drought (-0.19), and drought induces it in both genotypes; MKK3 is flat and not flagged. The cited passage supports its role in ABA and drought signalling. A flat MKK3 transcript says little, since MAPK cascades are regulated by phosphorylation.

Values match and the contrasts are read correctly: LOX3 is 2.63 log2 lower in watered BRL3ox and only 0.44 lower under drought, the largest such change among the lipoxygenases. Agrees with the paper's repressed JA-biosynthesis genes at basal conditions. Caveat: the baseline rests on two BRL3ox libraries; in roots LOX6 is the key enzyme.
statements.in_paper_where: Results 'Transcriptional control of metabolite production in BRL3ox' and Suppl. Fig. 8: JA biosynthesis genes repressed and JA lower at basal conditions. The release under drought is not stated.

statements.justification: Values match. Trehalose is higher in BRL3ox roots at day 0 (+1.60), as the paper reports. The smaller rise in BRL3ox (day 5 vs day 0: +0.60 vs +1.85) is what the uploaded columns show, though the paper describes steeper accumulation. The enzyme genes cited do not explain it: TRE1 unchanged, TPS7 lower.
statements.in_paper_where: Results 'BRL3ox plants accumulate osmoprotectant metabolites' (Fig. 4b, 4d, 4h) and Discussion (trehalose enzymes, Fig. 6c, d). The paper says accumulation under drought is steeper in BRL3ox, not smaller.

statements.justification: Values match. SUS3 is the most drought-induced gene of the pathway in WT (+3.23) and is higher in BRL3ox under drought (+0.79); sucrose is higher in BRL3ox at day 0 (+1.45). Both points are in the paper. The cited Sus1 study is on leaves and another isoform. Sucrose's smaller rise in BRL3ox is baseline-dependent.
statements.in_paper_where: Results (Fig. 4b: sucrose higher in BRL3ox roots; PaintOmics paragraph, Suppl. Fig. 11) and Discussion (SUS3 among enzymes regulated by BRL3 overexpression).

statements.justification: Watered repression is right and in the paper, but 'drought flips it' is not: the +2.37/+2.79/+2.01 are drought effects within BRL3ox; against WT under drought AOC1 (-2.35) and OPR3 (-0.99) stay repressed, and WT induces them too. LOX5 shows the opposite pattern and AOS is not a flagged gene (-0.63/-0.36).
statements.in_paper_where: Results 'Transcriptional control of metabolite production in BRL3ox' and Suppl. Fig. 8: JA biosynthesis genes repressed, JA lower at basal conditions.

statements.justification: TPS1 is not a flagged gene and none of its four values is above 0.50 log2, so 'drought-induced in BRL3ox but flat in WT' reads noise as a pattern. The rest is textbook background on trehalose 6-phosphate from a heat-tolerance study. The values are quoted correctly, but the statement tells nothing about this experiment.

Values match: A/N-InvC is lower in watered BRL3ox (-0.74) while sucrose is higher (+1.45). Reduced cleavage as a route to sucrose accumulation is a fair reading and fits the paper's deregulated sucrose metabolism. It rests on one invertase gene; nothing shown supports more 'synthesis', and the paper favours sugar import from shoots.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, PaintOmics paragraph (constitutive deregulation of sucrose metabolism, Suppl. Fig. 11) and Fig. 4b (sucrose higher in BRL3ox roots). The invertase link is not made.

overall.comment: Every quoted value matches the uploaded files and the four contrasts are mostly read correctly; unprompted, it recovers the primed sugar signature (trehalose and sucrose high at day 0), altered sucrose-cleaving genes and constitutively altered ABA and JA gene sets, so it touches all three of the paper's conclusions and adds the PYL/PP2C detail. It misses proline, raffinose and galactose metabolism (GolS2) and the TPPs, calls glucose BRL3ox-independent, misreads the JA genes as 'flipped' by drought, and reads trehalose and sucrose as less drought-induced in BRL3ox where the paper reports steeper accumulation (a consequence of the day-0 baseline). Several clauses are network-walk filler (TRE1 'hub', TPS1, MKK3) and the sugar statements repeat each other.
